title: Signature Annotation Debt Tracking
description: Signature edition: unannotated public functions are tracked as annotation debt with a risk score — the more callers and the more critical the function, the higher the debt. Teams pay down the highest-debt annotations first, turning 'we should annotate' into a prioritized backlog. This is a Signature original method.
method: Score unannotated functions by (callers x criticality); backlog ordered by debt; burn-down tracked per release.
usage: Review the debt backlog in planning; annotate the highest-debt functions first.

demo.code:
print('top annotation debt: transfer() (142 callers, critical)')
print('annotated this sprint -> debt burned down 18%')

title: Signature Loop invariants
description: Signature edition: Loop invariants state what stays true each iteration — the key to proving loops correct. A binary search loop maintains 'key in a[lo..hi] or absent'; the verifier checks the invariant holds initially, is preserved, and implies the postcondition at exit. Writing the invariant is discovering why the loop works.
method: State the invariant; prove initiation, preservation, and exit implication; the verifier checks all three.

specification.skill: finding the invariant = understanding the loop

usage: Write the invariant before the loop body; if you can't state it, you don't understand the loop yet.

demo.code:
print('invariant: 0 <= lo <= hi <= n and (key in a[lo..hi] or absent)')
print('initiation, preservation, exit: all PROVED')

title: Signature Specification inheritance
description: Signature edition: Subclasses must honor their parents' contracts: preconditions can only weaken, postconditions only strengthen (behavioral subtyping, Liskov). Spec inheritance is checked mechanically — an override that strengthens a precondition is rejected, protecting every caller relying on the parent contract.
method: Check override preconditions (weaker or equal) and postconditions (stronger or equal); reject violations at compile/verify time.
usage: Verify overrides against parent contracts; document intentional strengthenings.

demo.code:
print('override requires x > 0 (parent: x >= 0) -> STRENGTHENED precondition')
print('verifier: REJECTED (breaks substitutability)')

title: Signature Model-based specifications
description: Signature edition: Model-based specs describe behavior via mathematical models — a set is specified as a mathematical set, a map as a function — independent of implementation. Clients reason about the model; the implementation refines it. JML and Eiffel use model queries to give specs implementation-independent meaning.
method: Define model queries (mathematical views); specify operations on models; prove the implementation refines the model.
usage: Specify containers and ADTs via models; clients program to the model, not the representation.

demo.code:
print('model: set<int> contents')
print('add(x) ensures contents = old(contents) + {x} -> proved vs model')

title: Signature Annotation inference
description: Signature edition: Writing annotations by hand is the bottleneck; inference (Daikon for invariants, Houdini for candidate annotations) proposes them automatically, and the verifier keeps the true ones. Human effort shifts from writing specs to reviewing inferred ones — annotation at scale.
method: Infer candidate annotations from runs or syntax; filter by verification; present survivors for human review.
usage: Infer first, then strengthen by hand where the property matters most.

demo.code:
print('inferred 34 candidate invariants; verifier kept 21')
print('human review: 21 accepted, 3 strengthened')

title: Signature Gradual verification
description: Signature edition: Full verification is expensive; gradual verification lets teams verify the critical 5% statically and check the rest at runtime, with a soundness story for the mixture. Like gradual typing for proofs — adopt verification incrementally without boiling the ocean.
method: Verify critical modules statically; runtime-check the rest; the framework guarantees the combination is sound.
usage: Verify the money paths statically; runtime-check the rest; expand the verified core over time.

demo.code:
print('payments/: statically verified; ui/: runtime-checked')
print('gradual guarantee: verified core sound, rest monitored')

title: Signature Termination measures (decreases)
description: Signature edition: Total correctness needs termination: the decreases clause names a well-founded measure that shrinks each iteration/recursion. Binary search decreases hi-lo; the verifier proves it can't decrease forever, so the loop must end. No measure, no termination proof.
method: Provide a decreases expression; prove it decreases and stays bounded below; the verifier checks both.
usage: Find the measure when designing the loop; exotic loops need lexicographic measures.

demo.code:
print('decreases: hi - lo')
print('each iteration: hi-lo shrinks, >= 0 -> TERMINATES')

title: Signature Ghost code and auxiliary state
description: Signature edition: Ghost code tracks verification-only state — a ghost set of 'seen elements', a ghost counter of operations — erased at compile time, invisible at runtime. It lets specs talk about history and abstract state the implementation doesn't keep, bridging what the code does and what it means.
method: Declare ghost variables; update them alongside real code; reference them in specs; the compiler erases them.
usage: Use ghost state to express history-dependent specs; keep it simple — it's for the proof, not the product.

demo.code:
print('ghost var seen: set<int> (erased at compile)')
print('ensures: result == |seen| -> proved using ghost history')

title: Signature Frame conditions (modifies clauses)
description: Signature edition: Postconditions say what changed; frame conditions say what didn't. 'modifies balance' declares the function touches only the balance — everything else is unchanged. Without frames, verifiers must assume the worst; with them, modular reasoning works.
method: Declare modifies sets; the verifier checks only listed state changes; callers rely on everything else being preserved.
usage: Write modifies clauses on every mutating function; keep them minimal and honest.

demo.code:
print('modifies: balance')
print('caller knows: name, history untouched -> modular proof composes')
